decisions.executionNote: Begin left-arm approach to the mint clock, gradually orienting for a top grasp across its thin front-to-back dimension; right arm stays parked.
Retry with much smaller translation and rotation increments after the continuity rejection.
Continue a smooth, elevated left-arm approach and slow wrist reorientation, retaining elbow configuration.
Advance left wrist toward the clock while continuing the gradual downward-grasp orientation.
Continue approaching above the clock with clearance, aligning the jaw opening front-to-back.
Clock appears nearer/higher than the initial depth estimate. Raise the open gripper for clearance while finishing the downward approach orientation.
Increase clearance above the clock before centering; its pose may have shifted from incidental contact, so keep the jaws open.
Move above the clock's new resting position with the gripper open and nearly vertical; reassess jaw alignment before descending.
Center the vertical open gripper over the mint clock, accounting for the offset from link6 to the fingers.
Replan from the executed prefix with smaller increments and modest descent to retain arm continuity and overhead alignment.
Align the open jaws over the fallen clock using both views, moving slightly left and forward while lowering cautiously.
Lower more than advancing to restore reach margin after the IK interruption; keep the fingers open and move slowly toward the clock.
Use the wrist view to center the clock between the open fingers before a final shallow descent.
Make a shallow, mostly downward adjustment at the clock edge while maintaining continuity and open jaws.
Descent is obstructed by the clock face. Back off upward and tilt the approach slightly forward so the fingers can surround the body instead of pressing on it.
The wrist view now shows the clock centered within the open jaws. Descend gently along the tilted approach to engage its sides.
Close around the clock's rim at the present contact depth without further pushing down; verify retention visually on a gentle lift.
Test retention with a small upward and slightly rearward lift, keeping the left gripper fully closed.
The clock did not follow the test lift. Reopen and approach a narrower side chord of the rim, slightly inward and lower.
Advance and lower a few millimeters per step to straddle the near-side rim rather than the full clock diameter.
Shift the open gripper forward at constant height to bring both sides of the rim inside the jaws.
Fine-center the clock rim between the jaws with small lateral and forward adjustments before closing.
Close at the deeper rim contact, where the clock now lies between the jaw faces; keep the wrist stationary during closure.
Test the apparent rim grasp with a gentle upward/rearward motion while maintaining fully closed gripper command.
The rim slipped again. Reopen and change to a shallower, front-edge approach so the fingers can pinch the clock's thickness rather than its diameter.
Continue reorienting to grip the front edge across its thickness, lowering and retreating together to keep the open fingertips clear.
Finish the shallow front-edge orientation, keeping the tip region at roughly constant height while aligning laterally with the clock body.
Approach the visible clock thickness from the front, with a small lateral correction and gentle lowering to place one finger beneath the rim.
The lower open finger appears table-limited. Narrow the jaw spacing toward the clock thickness, then lower slightly to center the edge without pushing against the table.
Close fully at the shallow front-edge contact to capture the clock thickness, without further descent.
Lift gently with the gripper closed to check whether the clock edge or foot is retained.
The clock remains on the table. Reopen to a moderate gap and insert farther toward its edge, rather than closing at fingertip-only contact.
Withdraw to clear the face, level the approach, and lower the wrist before reinserting, aiming to place the lower finger beneath the body.
Use smaller withdrawal and leveling increments after the continuity guard, keeping the open fingers clear of the clock.
Clear the clock completely by withdrawing at fixed height, allowing the open jaws to reset before a level insertion.
Approach the now-exposed near foot and lower rim with a level gripper, using the narrower feature for a more secure grasp.
Reduce the opening to fit the exposed foot, then lower the level gripper so the narrow jaws can straddle it without the lower finger being table-limited.
Replan around the wrist limit with smaller forward/downward increments and a slight downward tilt, maintaining the narrowed opening near the exposed foot.
Clear the table contact and rotate the jaw opening sideways so the narrow foot can be grasped without a finger needing to pass beneath the tabletop.
Continue rotating the jaw opening sideways at a stationary, cleared wrist position.
Continue the smooth roll toward horizontal finger separation while keeping the elbow-up arm pose continuous.
Finish horizontal jaw alignment and lower toward the clearly visible near yellow foot, keeping the finger separation above the table.
Align the horizontal jaws with the near foot, lowering and pitching slightly down while approaching slowly.
Fine-align the exposed yellow foot between the horizontal fingers, with only a few millimeters of insertion and descent.
